clue.text: Hissing bird turned and left insect

indicators.note: something turned faces the other way, so the bird's name is read from its end

blocks.note: the ibis is a long-billed wading bird
L is the standard abbreviation for left
the ant is a common insect

explanation.surface: A hissing bird swings round and abandons the insect it was after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hissing' reads as a description of the bird, but it is the definition standing alone at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Sibilant describes a speech sound made with a hiss, such as s or sh, so it is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Instant alternative

blocks.note: first meaning: a moment, a very brief stretch of time

explanation.walkthrough: 'Instant alternative' looks like a quick substitute, but the two words are separate meanings of one noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A second is a tiny unit of time, and a second option is another choice besides the first.

clue.text: Exclude piece on universal merit in sedative

explanation.surface: Someone is kept out of a share of a general prize, all in the context of a sleeping drug.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places one piece above the next; U for universal comes from British film ratings.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbiturate is a class of drug that depresses the nervous system, long prescribed to calm patients or induce sleep.

clue.text: Caustic substance in tree

blocks.note: first meaning: quicklime, a burning white alkaline powder
second meaning: the linden, or a citrus tree

explanation.surface: Something corrosive has been found lodged in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sounds like a location, but here it only joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Quicklime is calcium oxide, which burns skin, and the same name belongs to the linden tree and the citrus fruit tree.

clue.text: Novelist showing dynamic front, unusually

indicators.note: done unusually means done in an odd way, so the preceding words come out in a strange order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Nancy Mitford was an English writer of comic novels such as The Pursuit of Love, one of the famous Mitford sisters.

clue.text: Gathers energy to return prize

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the joined letters are read from the end

blocks.note: people meet when they gather
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.walkthrough: 'prize' looks like a noun, a trophy, but it is the verb meaning to value highly.
explanation.definitionFit: To prize something is to value it highly, and esteem as a verb means to regard with respect.

clue.text: Were tests designed to keep one familiar with urban life?

explanation.definitionFit: Being streetwise means having the shrewdness needed to cope with the dangers of modern city surroundings.

clue.text: Put away in the attic

blocks.note: the end of the and the start of attic

explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' suggests storing things in the attic, but here it is slang for consuming food.
explanation.definitionFit: To put away food is an informal idiom for eating a large amount of it.

clue.text: Damage airman starts to appraise, slowly rattling instruments

the opening letters of these two words

explanation.walkthrough: AC, aircraftman, is a junior rank in Britain's Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: Maracas are paired gourd shakers filled with beads, played by shaking so they rattle in Latin music.

clue.text: Mercy one ordered in ritual

indicators.note: putting things in order means sorting them, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: A ceremony is a formal set of acts performed on a solemn occasion, which is what a ritual is.

clue.text: Hollow case, prosecutor's last

blocks.note: a crate is a packing case
the final letter of prosecutor

explanation.surface: A weak legal case is the prosecutor's final effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hollow case' reads as an empty argument in court, but 'Hollow' is the definition and 'case' is a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is a bowl-shaped depression in the ground, a hollow made by impact or volcanic action.

clue.text: Prisoner in rage got out of order in assembly

indicators.note: out of order means not in the right sequence, so the letters are jumbled

clue.text: Fix article, breaking nothing

blocks.note: a is the indefinite article
nil means zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Repair an item without breaking anything.

clue.text: Cry, dim hope renewed, for syringe

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient wails, faint hope restored, at the sight of the needle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypodermic is a needle and plunger used to inject drugs under the skin, the medical syringe.

clue.text: Hate man with brutality dispatching one

indicators.note: dispatching something sends it away, so the letter for one is removed

blocks.note: a man is a male
violence is brutality
I is the Roman numeral for one

clue.text: Appalling prohibition I'm lifting, filling a trunk

taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Time poorly occupied by game, second in town

explanation.surface: Someone spends their time in town badly, absorbed by a game and finishing second.
explanation.walkthrough: Tunbridge Wells is a spa town in Kent, south-east England; 'poorly' is British for ill.

clue.text: Conservative hurt by insulting campaign to win support

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative

insulting remarks are offensive

explanation.walkthrough: C for Conservative refers to Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm offensive is a deliberate campaign of friendliness designed to win people's favour or backing.

clue.text: Firm information about year in power

blocks.note: Co is short for company, a firm

Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.definitionFit: Cogency is the persuasive force of an argument, its power to convince.

clue.text: Staff brought up and established in county

clue.text: Golfer modified range, retaining good standard

blocks.note: taken as written

a norm is a standard

clue.text: Singer back in Scotland

back means the letters are taken from the end towards the start

blocks.note: the middle letters of the word

explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice, the part between soprano and tenor.

clue.text: Formerly working with church

explanation.surface: Someone used to have a job with the church.
explanation.walkthrough: CE stands for the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Once as an adverb means at some time in the past, which is the meaning of formerly.

clue.text: Close attention applied to book set in New York

explanation.walkthrough: 'Close attention' reads as one phrase, but 'Close' is the definition, meaning near.

blocks.note: taken as written

clue.text: Appeal to share
